videos.title: The Best Monopoly Strategy, Tested on 300 Million Games
videos.description_start:
I turned eight classic Monopoly strategies into computer players and made them play 312,898,560 games against each other. At a table of four, the best one won 43% of its games. The worst one won 3%.

The gap doesn't come from one clever trick. It comes from four common mistakes: being picky about what you buy, saving your cash, stopping at three houses, and refusing to trade. Then I let the computer tune every habit at once, to see how far a carefully tuned player can go and which color set is really worth fighting for.

Get the game: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DYK1ZH2D?tag=perfectplaysim-20 (affiliate link)

This one's for everyone who asked for Catan after the Risk video. I turned the six plans people argue about into players, added a regular player to compare them against, and made them play a little over 200 million games.

Knight Army and All Five tied for first, both at 57% against three regular players (a fair share is 25%). The port plan finished last at all 20 of its tables. The biggest single thing I found is settlements before cities, at 5:55.
